title: How does a submarine stay underwater without sinking forever?
sources: Naval Sea Systems Command Submarine Fundamentals

lines.text: How does a massive submarine weighing thousands of tons dive into the abyss and come back up safely?
lines.caps: How does a *submarine | dive without sinking *forever?

lines.text: Submarines master Archimedes' principle of buoyancy using giant chambers called ballast tanks.
On the surface, the ballast tanks are filled with air, making the submarine lighter than displaced water.
lines.caps: Tanks filled with *air | keep it floating on *top

lines.text: To submerge, large vents open at the bottom, flooding the tanks with heavy seawater until the sub sinks.
To hover at a fixed depth, operators balance water and air to achieve neutral buoyancy.
To surface, high-pressure compressed air blasts all the seawater out, shooting the vessel back upward.
lines.caps: Compressed air blasts the *water out | shooting it *upward!

lines.text: It is pure mechanical physics operating deep beneath the ocean waves.
